==Biography==

TheShy was a member of [[Anarchy]] in 2014, but in November he joined [[Team WE]] as a streamer. He stayed with them until May of 2017, when he left and joined [[Invictus Gaming]] as their alternate top laner. The team's [[LPL/2017_Season/Summer_Season|Summer Season]] was similar to their Spring Season and they finished 3rd with a 10-6 record. They did much better in the [[LPL/2017_Season/Summer_Playoffs|playoffs]] and finished 3rd with a victory over Team WE in the third place match. IG then participated in the [[2017 Season China Regional Finals]], but failed to make it to Worlds after Team WE got their revenge against them and beat them 3-2.

=== 2018 Season === 
TheShy and iG kick-started their season with a 3rd place finish in the [[Demacia Championship/2017 Season|Demacia Championship]], losing 2-1 to [[Snake Esports]] in the loser's semifinal. Just two weeks later saw the start of the [[LPL/2018 Season/Spring Season|LPL Spring Season]]. Despite a regular season series record of 18-1, with their only loss being against [[Royal Never Give Up]], this did not translate into success in the [[LPL/2018 Season/Spring Playoffs|Spring Playoffs]]. With TheShy himself sidelined due to a hand injury, Invictus Gaming were defeated 3-2 by RNG in the semifinals, this being followed by a 3-1 loss at the hands of [[Rogue Warriors]] in the third-place match. Although their performance could be considered a disappointment, their placement secured them a spot at [[Rift Rivals 2018/LCK-LPL-LMS|Rift Rivals 2018]].

A 3rd place finish in the [[Demacia Cup/2018 Summer|Demacia Cup]], this time losing to [[Bilibili Gaming]] in the loser's semifinal without TheShy, was followed by a successful showing at Rift Rivals. Now recovered from his hand injury, TheShy and the team won both of their group stage games, helping the LPL to an eventual triumph over the LCK in the final. Invictus Gaming once again achieved an 18-1 regular season record in the [[LPL/2018 Season/Summer Season|LPL Summer Season]], their sole loss again to RNG. Despite the similarity of the year's regular season performances, a successful showing in the [[LPL/2018 Season/Summer Playoffs|Summer Playoffs]], finishing runner-up to Royal Never Give Up after a tight 3-2 series, resulted in the team's qualification to the [[2018 Season World Championship]] on [[2018 Season/Championship Points/China|points]].

Invictus Gaming was placed in Group D for Worlds 2018, alongside [[Fnatic]], [[100 Thieves]], and [[G-Rex]]. The group stage round robin concluded with iG and Fnatic tied for 1st place at 5-1. The tiebreaker went in the favor of Fnatic, resulting in TheShy and the team being drawn against [[KT Rolster]] in the quarterfinals. A tense affair saw iG emerge victorious 3-2 and progress to the semifinals where they met [[G2 Esports]]. A more straightforward 3-0 series secured them a place in the finals. Awaiting their challenge were Group D counterparts, Fnatic. Invictus Gaming's convincing performance in the finals resulted in a 3-0 victory, and made them the first Chinese team to win a World Championship.

=== 2019 Season ===
TheShy and iG started the season with a strong showing in the LPL, placing 2nd in the [[LPL/2019 Season/Spring Season|LPL Spring Season]] en route to their first domestic win in the organization's history. TheShy and iG win 3-0 against [[JD Gaming]] in the finals, qualifying iG for the [[2019 Mid-Season Invitational]]. TheShy was named the Finals MVP of the 2019 Spring Split.

== Trivia ==
* His name was previously Kang Dong-geun (강동근).
* Previously known as a high rated {{ci|Riven}}, {{ci|Yasuo}}, and {{ci|Nidalee}} player in KR server before becoming a professional player.
* Known for his {{ci|Aatrox}}, {{ci|Jayce}}, {{ci|Fiora}}, {{ci|Vladimir}} and {{ci|Akali}} since [[2018 Season World Championship]].
* Invented a famous Riven combo now known as "The Shy Combo."
* Enjoys playing ARAM and says they sharpen his mechanics.<ref>[https://www.reddit.com/r/leagueoflegends/comments/9qfknn/for_all_of_the_aram_enthusiasts_you_have_1_more/ For all of the ARAM enthusiasts, you have 1 more player to be supporting to in this Worlds, which is The Shy.] ''reddit.com''</ref><ref>https://twitter.com/HeyMunchables/status/1717508427692331193 ''x.com''</ref>
* Often mistaken for fellow Korean top laner [[Shy]].
* Also known as a great and skilled {{ci|Kalista}} player in the top lane.
* Went to the same high school as [[Cat (Steven Kwon)|Cat]] and started playing League of Legends in Season 2 along with Cat.
* Enjoys playing piano.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=29_0zLw5E58] ''YouTube''</ref>
* His fans often joke about his performance, from ''TheShyt'' when he plays badly to ''TheChad'' when he plays especially well.
** Sometimes fans also jokingly called him ''TheSpy'', and made it as twitch emote where he wears a suit, black hat and disguises glasses
* In the [[LPL]], TheShy is sometimes refered to in Chinese as "Shy Ge", which translates to "Brother Shy" (Shy哥). However, it’s also a word play in that it sounds very similar to "Shuai Ge" (帅哥), which means "handsome guy".
* Good friends with [[Summit]], they went to the same school.
* Has a massive scar on his right arm from a surgery due to an accident in 2018, which is the main reason why TheShy always wears long sleeves or  jackets.
=== Statistics ===
* Reached 1000 kills in the LPL on February 26, 2022.
** The 29th player to reach 1000 kills in the LPL.
* Reached 1500 kills in the LPL on April 18, 2025.
** The 28th player and 5th toplaner to reach 1500 kills in the LPL.
* Reached 300 wins in the LPL on July 14, 2023.
** Was the 17th player to reach 300 wins in the LPL.
* Reached 500 games in the LPL on February 15, 2025
** The 28th player to reach 500 games in the LPL.
* Reached 600 games in the LPL on August 16, 2025
** The 20th player to reach 600 games in the LPL.
* Reached 3000 assists in the LPL on July 19, 2025.
** Was the 38th player to reach 3000 assists in the LPL.

=== Awards ===
* LPL 1st All-Pro Team x6 (Spring 2018, Spring 2019, Summer 2019, Spring 2020, Summer 2020, Split 3 2025)
* LPL 2nd All-Pro Team x2 (Spring 2022, Summer 2022)
* LPL 3rd All Pro Team x2 (Split 1 2025, Split 2 2025)
